attempts.r01: aborted: stale console script in the old image (fixed: python -m opentransit.build.cli)
attempts.r02: stopped by the operator before any check ran so the new rollback freshness rule could be merged

failed.failed_reload_preserves_old_serving_stat: Old serving state was intact (58468 of 58469 requests answered 200 by the old generation; one client-side connection error, cause not captured) and the pointer was restored to a fresh-token binding of the old generation, but the operator reported timeout rather than the worker rejection because one reload took about 16 minutes (3.7 GB hashed several times from the Windows file share) against the 900 s default. The worker later rejected the candidate with a failure ack. The harness now passes --timeout 3600, caps load at 4 desynchronised clients and records client error types. Needs a live rerun.
failed.inflight_requests_finish_on_old_generati: Harness analysis defect, not a product failure: the six load clients ran in lock-step behind the 0.35 s delay proxy, so the first new-generation request started only after every old request had finished and the boundary-based crossing count was 0. Engine-side evidence in the same run shows six requests started before the ack and completed after it on the old engine (check old_engine_saw_inflight_requests_complete_after_acknowledgement), 0 non-200 responses, 0 old-generation responses started after the boundary, and no pointer read errors across 350119 reads. The harness now classifies in-flight requests against the activation ack time and jitters the clients. Needs a live rerun to record a clean pass.
failed.rollback_succeeds_for_valid_previous_gen: The worker rejected the rollback candidate (factory_rejected) while the pointer was restored and requests kept answering from the serving generation. The API log shows generation_reload_failed kind=TimeoutError, most likely the 1.2 s candidate health check against a freshly restarted, cold engine after about 14 minutes of hashing. Not proven. Mitigations added: the harness warms the restarted engine, and failure acks now record the exception class (failureKind) so a rerun is conclusive. If it recurs, the candidate health check needs a bounded retry.

notes: After a timed-out or rejected activation the pointer token differs from the worker token; retirement is acknowledged under the worker token (replacedOperationToken in the activation ack), which the operator now reports as retiredOperationToken. Latent defect found while designing the gate and fixed with a test.

Rollback freshness rule (root decision): new candidates need current freshness; rollback accepts serviceable (current, aging, stale) and refuses expired freshness or lapsed coverage. Verified by the two refusal checks and the stale-eligibility check.
Per-reload hashing dominates: initial 536 s, failed reload 971 s, activation under load 815 s, rollback 843 s, with the 3 GB reference read from a Windows bind mount.
